extracted.intended_audience: scientists (Principal Investigators) and Public Information Officers preparing ESA/Hubble press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for scientists on producing ESA/Hubble press releases: purposes, audiences, release types, 14 newsworthiness criteria, scientific-writing standards, and required visual support. Emphasizes collaboration between the Principal Investigator and the Public Information Officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core Purpose: communicate scientific advances
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases serve as primary vehicles for communicating scientific advances to the press, decision-makers, mediators, scientists, and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use press releases to reach diverse audiences and increase awareness of science, the organization, and specific projects. They require close collaboration between the Public Information Officer and the Principal Investigator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration with Public Information Officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases require close collaboration between the Public Information Officer and the Principal Investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work jointly with the PIO throughout drafting, approval, and distribution to ensure accuracy, timeliness, and suitability for target audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal: increase awareness of science and scientific process
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase awareness of science and the scientific work process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize how science is done, not only the results, to educate audiences about methods and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal: increase awareness of the organization
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame messages to highlight the institution's role, capabilities, and contributions when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal: increase awareness of specific projects/instruments/missions
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase awareness of specific scientific projects, instruments, or missions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use releases to publicize instruments, missions, datasets, or project milestones and link to further resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release type: News releases
rubrics_metrics.description: News releases: Focus on one or more scientific discoveries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when there is a research finding or scientific result worth dissemination; prioritize clarity and newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release type: Photo releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Photo releases: Feature compelling imagery without major discoveries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to showcase high-quality images or visual material that attract attention even absent a major new scientific claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release type: Video releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Video releases: Broadcast-ready video news releases (VNRs) for television and websites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce video-formatted content suitable for broadcast and online embedding when visuals or motion add value.

rubrics_metrics.name: News criterion: timing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the story is timely — e.g., aligns with new results, events, or windows of public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: News criterion: relevance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine how relevant the story is to target audiences or current public discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: News criterion: proximity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider geographic, cultural, or topical closeness that makes the story more salient to audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: News criterion: implications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight broader consequences or significance of the findings for science, society, technology, or policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: News criterion: conflict resolution
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include elements that resolve scientific controversies or conflicts when applicable, showing how the work clarifies open questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: News criterion: human interest angles
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify human stories, personal perspectives, or relatable elements that connect readers emotionally to the science.

rubrics_metrics.name: News criterion: mystery elements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use intriguing unanswered questions or surprising findings to pique curiosity.

rubrics_metrics.name: News criterion: major scientific breakthroughs
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag and prioritize genuinely breakthrough results that substantially advance knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: News criterion: fresh perspectives on existing findings
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present new interpretations, re-analyses, or novel angles on previously reported work.

rubrics_metrics.name: News criterion: record-breaking achievements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize firsts, records, or benchmark-setting results that are newsworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: News criterion: 'sexy topics' (e.g., black holes, exoplanets)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that certain topics naturally attract wider attention and may raise newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: News criterion: aesthetic appeal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the visual or sensory attractiveness of images, figures, or phenomena that can boost coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: News criterion: publication in distinguished journals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication in high-profile journals can increase the story's credibility and news appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: News criterion: cross-linking opportunities
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for opportunities to tie the release to other stories, datasets, missions, or institutional communications for amplified reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific writing: simplify complex concepts
rubrics_metrics.description: Simplify complex concepts for general audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate technical content into accessible language without misrepresenting the science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific writing: match explanations to audience comprehension
rubrics_metrics.description: Match explanations to target group comprehension levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust technical depth and jargon depending on whether the audience is journalists, policymakers, scientists, or the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific writing: define abbreviations and technical terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Define all abbreviations and technical terminology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid unexplained acronyms; provide plain-language definitions at first use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific writing: structure from foundational to complex
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure arguments from foundational to complex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build narratives that introduce basic concepts first, then layer in complexity to aid comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific writing: edit rigorously for clarity and accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Edit rigorously for clarity and accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prune ambiguity, correct errors, and ensure scientific claims are precisely stated and supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific writing: conduct thorough research before drafting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarize yourself with background literature, related work, and media context to write responsibly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific writing: maintain consistency in style and grammar
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain consistency in style and grammar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a consistent editorial style (spelling, tense, punctuation) to present a professional, readable release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required visual support
rubrics_metrics.description: High-quality accompanying images, illustrations, or videos are practically mandatory for success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide high-resolution images, clear illustrations, or broadcast-ready video to increase pick-up and impact; lack of visuals significantly reduces chances of coverage.
